lessons: Pack 2's late picks (Walking Corpse, two Wooden Stake, Maw of the Mire) and pack 3's Mulch and Gnaw to the Bone are guide-listed skips that left my WG with thin filler; take removal or a flier instead.
Tonight's 9 Forest/7 Plains WG with two Avacyn's Pilgrim went 1-2, so the guide's 9/8 'not doomed' line is weak support; give white 8 real sources.
The two 0-2 losses ran 26 to 32 turns with my only fliers, Abbey Griffin and Voiceless Spirit, unable to close, so take a third evasive threat over a third ground creature.
I took Sever the Bloodline first, then cut all black, yet both BR decks went 2-1 against me, so check whether an early strong pick's colour is still open before committing away from it.
My UG deck had almost no removal beyond Lost in the Mist, and Victim of Night, Dead Weight and Tribute to Hunger beat my bodies, so prioritise cheap removal over vanilla green and blue creatures.
Games ran 36 and 46 turns and my UG deck had no reliable closer, so take evasive finishers like Stitched Drake and Moon Heron over filler creatures.

Moment of Heroism doubled and Rebuke, Geistflame, Brimstone Volley and Slayer of the Wicked won my 3-0 WR deck, so the guide's 'cheap fliers plus removal' plan held; take Silverchase Fox and Spectral Rider over filler early.

Pick Gallows Warden and Village Bell-Ringer-style cheap humans over Ghoulcaller's Bell and Curse of the Pierced Heart; the guide's curse-skipping advice was right, since my curses sat in the sideboard.

Against the WU Round 3 deck with Smite the Monstrous and Rebuke, hold Brimstone Volley for fliers like Murder of Crows, as the guide advises; I dropped game 3 to Smite and Silent Departure, so keep a Blazing Torch-level answer for Angel of Flight Alabaster.

Round 1's 0-2 loss to the WR aggro deck (Brimstone Volley, Reckless Waif, Silverchase Fox) came from games that went 13-14 turns, so draft cheap early blockers before stacking top-end like Manor Gargoyle.
The UG deck's wins came from Lantern Spirit, Prey Upon, Spidery Grasp, and Essence of the Wild, which carried the 46-turn, 26-turn, and 30-turn games, so prioritise removal and evasive threats.
Taking a second Naturalize at pick 11 was wasted, since the extra copy was cut; take a playable creature or fixing instead of a duplicate situational card.

Once black was set, I took Abbey Griffin, Voiceless Spirit and Abbey Griffin in pack 2 picks 2-4 and played none, leaving Falkenrath Noble and Vampire Interloper (which cannot block) as my only fliers.
My 2-1 BR ran only 12 creatures, below the guide's 14-16 norm, and lost round 1 1-2 in 15- to 17-turn grinds; count creatures before adding another removal spell.
Play the removal you draft: I took Claustrophobia third in pack 3 and benched it, then lost round 2 1-2 to WU fliers like Murder of Crows and Angel of Flight Alabaster.
I drafted without a guide and left Blasphemous Act and Curse of Oblivion out, so late picks went to dead cards; take playable BR creatures or removal over speculative auras.
Expect Smite the Monstrous: WU ran two, and it punishes my power-4+ top end like Geistcatcher's Rig, so keep cheap creatures and answers to fliers in the deck.
The guide calls Delver of Secrets weak, and I maindecked it anyway. Take a cheap white or blue flier or a playable removal spell over it.

Round 3's WR deck, which went 3-0 and beat me 2-1, ran Chapel Geist, Rebuke, Bonds of Faith and two Silverchase Fox. When white fliers are contested, pick up Slayer of the Wicked and keep a second colour open.

My matches ran long (26, 30, 27 turns), so favour cheap evasive threats over slow filler like Mausoleum Guard. The guide's claim that WU fliers are the strongest lane did not hold up in a crowded draft.
Prioritise real removal over bodies: my UB deck ran only three answers, while the BR decks beat me with Dead Weight, Tribute to Hunger and Geistflame.
Stop spending late picks on Curse of Oblivion: I took three across packs 1 and 2 and played none of them.
I took Rolling Temblor at pick 6 and benched it, but seat 5 registered it against me; play a colour's removal over a marginal creature.
